sections.html:
In Southwest Virginia, on the Roanoke River within the Blue Ridge, sits Roanoke, an independent city roughly 250 miles southwest of Washington, D.C. along Interstate 81. Its 2025 estimate of 99,111 residents trails the 100,011 of 2020 slightly. No Virginia city west of Richmond is larger, and it anchors a metro area of 315,251 people.

Almost every one of its 42.85 square miles is land, and the elevation is 974 feet. Mill Mountain, a 1,700-foot peak with a 500-acre municipal park, rises within the city and carries the 88.5-foot Roanoke Star, source of the nickname Star City of the South.

Roanoke started as the small town of Big Lick. In 1882 the Norfolk and Western Railway chose it for its headquarters and shops, and within two years it was the City of Roanoke. Population grew 22 times over in the 1880s, and later annexations from Roanoke County added more land.

Houses on the older blocks near downtown come from that boom, so age and deferred maintenance are common topics for sellers there. Parts of the former industrial land south of downtown have been redeveloped since the locomotive shops closed.

Roanoke has 49 neighborhoods, and the comprehensive plan aims to grow each into a village with its own center, with downtown as the hub for all of them. Raleigh Court, near Grandin Village, is held up as a model, with housing clustered around a commercial district anchored by the Grandin Theatre.

The National Register of Historic Places lists nine of them, in whole or in part. Think your address might fall in one? Check with the city prior to any exterior work.

Raleigh Court is the neighborhood planners point to when they describe the village idea. Houses there sit around a small commercial district anchored by the Grandin Theatre, the city's only surviving historic theater. Buyers who like walking to shops and a movie will respond to that, so a seller on those streets should lead with it. The same goes for a house within reach of Patrick Henry High School.

Newer or plainer blocks have a different pitch. There the selling points are price, lot size and quick access to Interstate 81. Whatever the street, describe the house the way a buyer will search for it.

Heavy rain, often from the remnants of a hurricane, runs off the surrounding hills into the narrow Roanoke Valley, and flooding has been the city's main weather hazard. Start by learning whether your parcel is close to the river or a creek, then check crawl spaces and basements for water lines. Save paperwork on any flood claim or drainage job. For floodplain rules on your lot, the city is the place to ask.

Roanoke has four mild seasons. Snowfall averages 14.8 inches a winter, and a December 2009 storm once dropped 17 inches in one event. Summers are humid, with about 30.5 days a year at 90 degrees or higher. That wears on roofs, gutters and wood decks, and a freeze can split pipes in a house with no heat. A quick walk-through of an empty house shows where you stand.

sections.h2: Health care and the medical district
sections.html: Health care leads the local economy. Carilion Clinic employs more than 13,000 people, making it both the top employer in the city and the biggest private one west of Richmond. Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine and Research Institute opened in 2007, and Radford University Carilion was established in 2019. Hospital and university jobs draw renters and buyers who often want to live near the medical district, so mention it if your house is nearby.

sections.h2: Parks and trails as a selling point
sections.html: Outdoor access is part of how the city markets itself. The valley holds 26 miles of greenways, the Blue Ridge Parkway passes just south, and Carvins Cove, at 12,700 acres, ranks as the third-largest municipal park in America. Living near a trailhead, greenway or park gives you something concrete to tell buyers.

Roanoke City Public Schools operates two general enrollment high schools: Patrick Henry in the Raleigh Court area and William Fleming in Northwest Roanoke. Higher education includes Virginia Western Community College in the city, with Roanoke College next door in Salem.

sections.h2: What happens at a Roanoke closing
sections.html: Closing is a signing session: the deed and a settlement statement. Out of the price come any mortgage payoff, tax owed and recording fees, and you keep the remainder. With a cash buyer, nobody schedules an appraisal or waits for loan approval, so the closing date usually holds. An itemized estimate in advance tells you your net before you commit.

sections.h2: Selling an empty or inherited house
sections.html: Empty through a mountain winter, a house can hide burst pipes, damp crawl spaces or a roof that leaked. Walk it, jot down what you notice and collect repair and insurance papers. Heirs should also gather proof of their authority to sign. When the buyer accepts the place as is, there are no contractors to hire and no work to supervise from afar.

A regular listing may fetch the top price for a house in good shape if you can sit through showings, inspection repairs and a buyer's loan process. Cash gives up some of that upside in return for speed and certainty, a fair trade for an estate, a tenant, a transfer or a house needing more work than you want. Weigh what lands in your account after taxes, repairs and carrying costs, not the advertised price.

sections.h2: What does a Roanoke seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
Virginia sets its grantor tax at 50 cents per $500 of the price. It lands on the seller by default, the buyer can agree to cover part or all, and the clerk certifies payment before recording the deed. See Virginia Code 58.1-802.

The real estate valuation and treasurer offices can give you current rates, due dates and appeal steps. Tax still owed comes out of your proceeds when you settle.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Roanoke
sections.html:
Contract, title search and deed work the same way in a cash sale as in any Roanoke sale. Only the lender drops out.

  • Describe the house and your target closing date.
  • We look it over, and an offer reflects its current condition.
  • A settlement company handles the title search and deed.
  • You sign, get paid and give up the keys.

Nothing needs repairing or cleaning out beforehand, and declining costs you nothing. Take a photo ID, your deed if you have it and mortgage details. With an inherited house, add the papers showing who may sign for the estate.

faqs.q: What is the population of Roanoke, VA?
faqs.a: Roanoke is estimated at 99,111 residents for 2025, against 100,011 in the 2020 census.
Flooding has been the city's main weather hazard, and the worst flood came on November 4, 1985. A flood reduction project was finished in 2012.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Roanoke?
faqs.a: Carilion Clinic is the top employer and the largest private employer west of Richmond, with more than 13,000 employees.

faqs.q: How many neighborhoods does Roanoke have?
faqs.a: There are 49 neighborhoods, and the National Register of Historic Places lists nine of them in whole or in part.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Roanoke house without repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can buy the house as is, and you do not need to fix anything first.
